summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and then said outright that the task was **bounded**. It showed a short design in chat, never wrote a spec document, got approval, and edited app.js. The escalation criteria (2–4) fail.
reasoning: The story's goal was for the router to send this ambiguous "add a param" brief down the architectural path. It did not. After reading the code, the agent wrote: "Classifying this as **bounded** — `login` already exists in `app.js` with one call site... But it changes a function signature". It asked one AskUserQuestion about where userId should come from. I picked its recommended option, which returns userId from login and keeps the signature. It then gave an in-chat design and, once I approved it, edited app.js. No docs/ directory was ever created. It flagged the signature-change concern itself but did not escalate. Criterion 1 passes, criterion 5 passes, and criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail.

observations.description: Router misclassification: the agent said the change "changes a function signature" and named the options-object choice "the expensive-to-reverse one", yet it still chose bounded rather than architectural.

The agent steered the user away from the requested parameter change (recommending "Return it from login" and keeping the signature). That shrank the scope and made bounded look right after the fact. The router classified before this scoping question was asked; it could classify after it instead.
The Claude Code trust and bypass-permissions dialogs start with "No, exit" selected. This is minor setup friction for the harness.
Good behavior: the agent checked the change with `node --check` and said openly that it had not loaded index.html in a browser. It made no commit.

criteria.evidence: Session log 48c1b8e6...jsonl: the first tool call is {"tool":"Skill","in":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\",...}"}. It comes before the Edit on app.js.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in the log: "Classifying this as **bounded**". `find coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". `git status --short` showed only " M app.js".

criteria.criterion: Spec document presented for review before implementation
criteria.evidence: No spec file exists. The review step was an in-chat design ending "Say the word and I'll make the change." The log shows no Write to any specs path; the only file change is an Edit to app.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It did exactly that: "Classifying this as **bounded**", followed by an in-chat "Design, then I'll stop for your yes." No spec file was written.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: The classification text says "bounded". The screen and log show no probe plan or spike wording.
